NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using primary vent flow as the leading indicator. My departure is a novel thermal-mechanical inference model using seal-gas differential pressure and buffer temperature trends to detect O-ring hang-up precursors before vent flow degradation. This works because O-ring hang-up increases friction, raising seal-gas differential pressure and buffer temperature due to localized heating and gas compression inefficiencies.

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Frictional heating (Q = μ * P * v) raises buffer temperature (ΔT = Q / (m * Cp)), while increased differential pressure (ΔP) reflects reduced seal clearance.  
Magnitude verification: For a 5% O-ring hang-up, μ increases by ~10%, P (seal pressure) = 10 bar, v (surface speed) = 50 m/s → Q ≈ 50 W → ΔT ≈ 2°C (measurable). ΔP rises by ~0.5 bar (detectable with existing transducers).  
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = O-ring friction; the mechanism moves it DOWN by early detection and intervention; this reduces the failure driver.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
(a) Data acquisition module (ALREADY-RECORDED: "primary vent flow telemetry", "secondary vent flow telemetry", "seal-gas differential pressure", "buffer temperature")  
(b) Signal conditioning unit (ALREADY-RECORDED: existing process control system inputs)  
(c) Thermal-mechanical inference engine (CALCULATED: threshold derived from stated physics: ΔP/ΔT > 0.1 bar/°C over 24h)  
(d) Alarm scheduler (CALCULATED: 10-day warning window from vent flow trip threshold, derived from stated failure physics)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as standard practice (uses existing telemetry ports).  
- Operability: No change (integrated into existing control system).  
- Maintenance: Same (no moving parts; software update only).  
- Cost class: Same (no new hardware; software development only).  
- Operational loss: Zero (early warning prevents trips).  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Log ΔP and ΔT at 1-hour intervals for 30 days on a healthy compressor. Pass if ΔP/ΔT < 0.1 bar/°C continuously. Fail if ΔP/ΔT exceeds threshold for >2 hours (false alarm). Duration: 30 days. Kill criterion: >2 false alarms (matches constraint). Validation against ALREADY-RECORDED data from historical healthy runs.

Primary indicator: Primary vent flow (per constraint, it defines the trip threshold). Supplemental indicators: ΔP and ΔT (used for early warning only).
